selection.rust: Additional reuse candidates rejected after mixed end-to-end measurements; numerical source and bridge restored to before.

candidate_a.description: Both engines reuse noise and prepared references; Rust matches via ndarray row views.

ablation.scope: Warm full reviews on the final source; the previous corrected-signal reuse remains enabled. One warm-up per engine; four modes in rotating order over five repeats. All report hashes identical within engine.

paired_full_review.scope: Actual previous/current source in two persistent worker processes per engine, each with decoded inputs and one warm-up. Nine adjacent pairs, alternating which revision goes first. Only one worker computes at a time. Wall timings include validation, analysis and report construction, excluding input read, startup and report serialization. Other machine workloads remain uncontrolled.

conditions: Same private acquisition/library, macOS arm64, four numerical thread environment variables set to 1; no concurrent agent benchmark/build/test work. Other applications were using the machine; power mode and background workload were not controlled. OS caches retained; compilation excluded.
limitations: Full-review reuse is the intended optimization. No single-analysis speedup or stable startup/memory improvement is claimed. Both Rust candidate overall paired-run medians were slightly slower, although candidate B won 7/9 adjacent pairs. The mixed results did not justify retaining the added Rust interface changes. Report equivalence preserves behavior, not independently verified chemical identity.
